description: If the current app is available, use its json.dumps method for serialization; otherwise, fallback to json.dumps from the standard json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.dump method to serialize and write to a file; otherwise, fallback to json.dump from the standard json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.loads method for deserialization; otherwise, fallback to json.loads from the standard json module. The data must be a string or UTF-8 bytes.

If the current app is available, use its json.load method to deserialize data from a file; otherwise, fallback to json.load from the standard json module. The file must be opened in text mode or binary mode with UTF-8 bytes for deserialization.
Serialize the given arguments as JSON and return a flask.Response object with the application/json mimetype. This operation requires an active app context.
Writing to a file must use text mode with UTF-8 encoding to be valid JSON when using the dump method.
The application must have a `static_folder` defined to serve static files correctly.
The application can only be run using `app.run()` if it has not been invoked from Flask's command line interface to avoid blocking CLI commands.
The configuration for `SERVER_NAME` must be explicitly set to enable subdomain routing and must not depend on default values.
The return value from request handlers must be a valid response type, which can be either a string, bytes, dict, list, tuple, or a response object.
If `max_age` is set to None, the browser should utilize conditional requests instead of a timed cache to optimize resource retrieval.
If any registered `before_request` handler returns a non-None value, processing of the request must terminate immediately, returning that value as the response.
If `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` is set to False and the application is not in debug mode, exceptions raised by view functions will not propagate, preventing error details from being outputted to clients.
View functions must not return None or types that are not recognized as valid response objects to ensure a consistent response structure.
In debug mode, Flask will present a complete stack trace of exceptions that occur during request handling to enhance debugging capabilities.
When the `load_dotenv` option is enabled (set to True), the application must load `.env` and `.flaskenv` files to set environment variables accordingly.
The `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` configuration parameter must be set to True to enhance security by preventing client-side scripts from accessing cookies.
Static files will only be served if the `static_folder` is correctly defined and configured, ensuring proper handling of these resources.
All registered request teardown functions will be executed, regardless of whether an exception was encountered during the request, ensuring consistent cleanup actions.
Errors occurring during request teardown will be collected and raised if encountered, ensuring that exceptions are properly managed and reported.
An error must be raised if `make_response` receives an invalid response type from a view function to ensure the validity of responses.
URLs generated through the `url_for` function may include an anchor if specified using the `_anchor` argument, facilitating navigation to specific sections of a page.
Automatic options responses must be provided by the application if `provide_automatic_options` is set to True and the request method is OPTIONS to support method discovery compliance.
The application must validate the consistency between `static_host` and `host_matching` when adding a static route to ensure proper routing behavior.
The 'static_folder' must be set to serve static files; otherwise, a RuntimeError is raised.
Resources can only be opened for reading; valid modes are 'r', 'rt', and 'rb'. Opening in any other mode raises a ValueError.
The default configuration for SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is 'None', which tells the browser to use conditional requests instead of a timed cache.
If SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is set and is a timedelta, its value should be returned in seconds; if it is not set or is None, None should be returned.
If SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is an integer, it is to be returned directly without further modifications.
A route is automatically registered for the view function serving static files at 'static_url_path' when 'static_folder' is set.
A Flask application must be specified using the '--app' option, the 'FLASK_APP' environment variable, or by having a 'wsgi.py' or 'app.py' file in the current directory.
If multiple Flask applications are detected in a module, a NoAppException will be raised, requiring the user to specify the correct one explicitly.
A factory function for creating a Flask application must be callable without arguments; if it cannot be called as such, a NoAppException is raised.
If the specified application name does not correspond to a valid attribute name or valid function call, a NoAppException will be raised.
The environment variable 'FLASK_DEBUG' controls whether the application runs in debug mode. If not set, debug mode defaults to 'False'.
If the debug option is not explicitly set during command execution, it will default to the current value of the 'FLASK_DEBUG' environment variable.
The command to launch the development server ('run') is solely for development purposes and is not suitable for production environments.
The command 'routes' displays all registered routes in the application, along with their associated methods and endpoints.
A command will always execute within the application's application context when using the decorator 'with_appcontext'.
When using SSL, if the '--key' option is provided, the '--cert' option must also be specified to ensure secure connections.
The application context for commands must be loaded unless it is already active, maintaining context across command invocations to ensure stability.
If an error occurs while loading the application, it will propagate immediately unless in a reloading scenario, in which case the error will be displayed while allowing server operation.
The application must be properly initialized before executing any commands that require server operations, such as 'run' or 'shell'.
The loading of environment variables from '.env' or '.flaskenv' files is managed by the 'load_dotenv_defaults' parameter, which defaults to True and can be overridden by the user.
The 'after_this_request' function can only be used when a request context is active (e.g., within a route handler).
The 'copy_current_request_context' function can only be used when a request context is active (e.g., within a route handler).
Accessing the 'request' property of the AppContext raises a RuntimeError if there is no associated request object in the context.
Accessing the 'session' property of the AppContext raises a RuntimeError if there is no associated request object in the context.
The push method of the AppContext engages request matching only if the context was not previously pushed.
The pop method of the AppContext raises a RuntimeError if it is not the active context or if it has been pushed more times than it has been popped.
The function has_request_context returns True when a request context is active; otherwise, it returns False.
The function has_app_context returns True when an app context is active; otherwise, it returns False.
The constructor of AppContext initializes the context with the request and session parameters set to None if not provided.
The session object is loaded the first time it is accessed instead of being loaded when the context is pushed.
Teardown functions are triggered when the context is popped, depending on whether it is a request or app context.
A JSONProvider must implement the :meth:`dumps` and :meth:`loads` methods to support serialization and deserialization of JSON data.
Either positional or keyword arguments can be provided to the :meth:`response` method, but both cannot be used at the same time.
If no arguments are given to the :meth:`response` method, then ``None`` is serialized as JSON.
The response output is in the ``application/json`` mimetype as specified in the :meth:`response` method.
The :meth:`response` method serializes the provided arguments as JSON and returns a Response object containing the serialized data.
The :meth:`dumps` method sorts keys in any serialized dictionaries if the ``sort_keys`` attribute is set to True.
The ``default`` method must either return a valid JSON type or raise a ``TypeError`` when serialization fails on unsupported types.
The :meth:`loads` method deserializes data from a string or bytes, returning the resulting Python object.
The ``compact`` attribute controls the formatting of the response output based on its value and the application's debug mode.
The ``ensure_ascii`` attribute determines whether non-ASCII characters are replaced with escape sequences during JSON serialization.
The :meth:`dumps` method must apply default serialization behaviors defined by the attributes of JSONProvider, including ``default``, ``ensure_ascii``, and ``sort_keys``.
Files must be opened for writing with UTF-8 encoding to ensure valid JSON is written when using the :meth:`dump` method.
The :meth:`load` method deserializes data that is read from a file opened for reading text or UTF-8 bytes.
Date instances will be serialized to HTTP date format using the ``default`` method during JSON serialization.
Instances of UUID and decimal types are converted to their string representations using the ``default`` function during JSON serialization.
Instances of dataclass types are serialized to dictionaries using ``dataclasses.asdict`` during serialization.
A session is considered permanent if the '_permanent' key is explicitly set to True in the session dictionary.
The 'new' flag for a session is always set to False, indicating that the session cannot reliably determine if it is newly created.
The modified flag for a session must be set to True whenever session data is changed, including modifications to mutable data types within the session.

The accessed flag indicates whether the session has been accessed at least once, regardless of whether it was modified. This flag is set when the session object is accessed through the request context.

A Set-Cookie header should be included in the response for the session cookie if the session is modified, or if the session is marked as permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is set to True in the configuration.
A null session object will be generated when the open_session method fails or returns None, allowing read-only access while modifications will raise an error with a descriptive message.
The name of the session cookie is retrieved from the application configuration using app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_NAME'].
The domain attribute for the session cookie is determined by the value in app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN'].
The path for which the session cookie is valid is established using the value from app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_PATH']. If not set, it defaults to app.config['APPLICATION_ROOT'].
The status of the HttpOnly attribute for the session cookie is derived from app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY'].
The secure attribute for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE'].
The SameSite attribute for the session cookie is configured using the value in app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE'].
The partitioned attribute for the session cookie is derived from the configuration variable app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED'].
The expiration time of the session is calculated based on whether the session is marked as permanent and the application's configured permanent_session_lifetime.
If the session is empty and it has been modified, the corresponding Set-Cookie header should include a directive to delete the cookie from the response.
A cookie for the session will only be set if the session is not empty and is either marked as modified or if SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is enabled in the application configuration.
Signals are generated for various stages of the Flask application lifecycle to facilitate internal communication within the application.
The signal 'template-rendered' indicates a template has been rendered successfully.
The signal 'before-render-template' indicates that a template is about to be rendered.
The signal 'request-started' signifies the beginning of request processing.
The signal 'request-finished' indicates that request processing has been completed successfully.
The signal 'request-tearing-down' indicates that the request context is being torn down to allow cleanup operations.
The signal 'got-request-exception' indicates that an exception has occurred during the request processing.
The signal 'appcontext-tearing-down' indicates that the application context is being destroyed and triggers any associated cleanup routines.
The signal 'appcontext-pushed' indicates that a new application context has been pushed onto the context stack.
The signal 'appcontext-popped' indicates that the top application context has been removed from the context stack.
The signal 'message-flashed' indicates that a notification message has been sent to the user, typically for alerts or confirmations.
The base_url must be absent, or if provided, it cannot coexist with subdomain or url_scheme.
If base_url is None, it is constructed from the server name (SERVER_NAME) and application root (APPLICATION_ROOT).
If subdomain is provided, the server name is prepended with the format '{subdomain}.{server_name}'.
If url_scheme is None, it defaults to the application's preferred URL scheme (PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME).
The REMOTE_ADDR in the environment base is set to '127.0.0.1'.
The HTTP_USER_AGENT in the environment base is set to include the Werkzeug version string.
A session transaction can be initiated using a with statement, allowing modifications to the session being used during that context.
Cookies must be enabled for session transactions to proceed; if disabled, a TypeError is raised.
If the session backend fails to open a session, a RuntimeError is raised.
The invoke method for FlaskCliRunner defaults to the application's CLI group if no CLI command is provided.
If 'obj' is not provided in the kwargs while invoking a CLI command, a ScriptInfo instance is automatically passed to it.
